chunks: He said: Abul Hasan Ali ibn Bilal al-Mahlabi reported to me from Abu al-Abbas Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Baghdadi, who reported from Muhammad ibn Ismail, who reported from Muhammad ibn al-Salt, who reported from Abu Kudainah, from Ata, from Saeed ibn Jubair, from Abdullah ibn al-Abbas, who said:

When the verse "Indeed We have given you al-Kawthar" was revealed to the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, Ali ibn Abi Talib, peace be upon him, asked him: "O Messenger of Allah, what is al-Kawthar?" He said: "It is a river with which Allah has honoured me." Ali, peace be upon him, said: "Indeed this river is sacred, so describe it for us, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "Yes, O Ali, al-Kawthar is a river that flows beneath the Throne of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Its water is whiter than milk, sweeter than honey, and softer than cream. Its pebbles are of aquamarine, ruby, and coral. Its grass is saffron, its soil is fragrant musk, and its foundations are beneath the Throne of Allah, Mighty and Majestic."

Then the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him and his family, struck his hand on the side of the Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, and said: "O Ali, indeed this river is for me, for you, and for those who love you after me."

key_terms.أَمِير الْمُؤْمِنِين: Commander of the Faithful, title of Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (AS)
key_terms.الْكَوْثَر: Al-Kawthar: literally "the Abundance", a river in Paradise promised to the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW)
key_terms.عَرْش: The Throne of Allah, the greatest of God's creations

ai.seo_question: What is al-Kawthar and how did Prophet Muhammad describe it to Imam Ali?
ai.summary: This hadith describes al-Kawthar, the heavenly river mentioned in Surah 108 of the Quran. Through a dialogue between the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) and Imam Ali (AS), the Prophet provides a vivid description of this river in Paradise -- with water whiter than milk, sweeter than honey, pebbles of precious gems, grass of saffron, and soil of musk, all beneath the Throne of God. The hadith concludes with the Prophet declaring that this river belongs to him, Ali, and those who love Ali after him.
word_analysis: and for those who love you
